open_points.subject: prepare_request plain-HTTP instance-class validation
open_points.text: - prepare_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] A plain http base_url is allowed only when instance_class is in the imported PLAIN_HTTP_INSTANCE_CLASSES constant, an instance_class that is None or not a known class counting as the imported DEFAULT_INSTANCE_CLASS constant, or when the base_url host is a loopback IP address literal; any other plain http target gives plain_http_not_allowed; the host judged is always the base_url host, never a required Host header.
open_points.other_text:
IMPORTED DATA ACCESS SIGNATURES (constants from the imports above — read them, never redefine them; their values are not part of this context):
DEFAULT_INSTANCE_CLASS: str
INSTANCE_SETTABLE_HEADER_NAMES: tuple[str, ...]
KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES: tuple[str, ...]
PLAIN_HTTP_INSTANCE_CLASSES: tuple[str, ...]
RELEASE_CEILING_FAILURE_DETAIL_BYTES_MAX: int
RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX: int
RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX: int
RELEASE_CEILING_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS: int
open_points.question: The rule requires deciding whether instance_class is “not a known class,” but no imported constant supplies the set of known instance classes. Must that condition be removed or must a known-instance-classes constant be added to IMPORTS?
